MEMORANDUM (D4, D6, rq1). Cited as proved (answer:work:003-struct-core-v2): at every non-root vertex, mutation at the max d strictly lowers d; mutations at a,b,c raise the max to >= (4ab-1)d >= 3d; the quotient graph is a tree rooted at v_0=(1,1,1,1); every vertex has <= 3 children (fewer when coordinates coincide), the root has exactly 1.

T1 (depth upper). Each child edge multiplies the max by >= 3, so d >= 3^{depth(v)} and depth(v) <= log_3 d.

T2 (crude count). N(H) <= sum_{0<=k<=floor(log_3 H)} 3^k = (3^{floor(log_3 H)+1} - 1)/2 <= (3H-1)/2. N(H) = O(H), constant 3/2.

T3 (depth lower). Child max = 4*(product of other three) - x <= 4bcd <= 4d^3. Let L_k = max of log_2 d at depth k: L_{k+1} <= 3L_k + 2, L_0 = 0, so L_k + 1 <= 3(L_{k-1} + 1), giving L_k <= 3^k - 1. Hence depth(v) >= log_3(log_2 d + 1). Two-sided: log_3(log_2 d + 1) <= depth(v) <= log_3 d.

T4 (rq1 dichotomy; Outcome A holds). (i) The a=b=1 locus is a single chain. Equation: 2 + c^2 + d^2 = 4cd. The parent of (1,1,c,d) is the re-sorted (1,1,c,d'), d' = (c^2+2)/d < d, again with a=b=1; descending to the root and inverting gives the chain v_0=(1,1,1,1), v_1=(1,1,1,3), v_{j+1} = (1,1,d_j,4d_j - c_j) with c_{j+1}=d_j, i.e. d_{j+1} = 4d_j - d_{j-1}, ratio r_j = 4 - 1/r_{j-1} increasing from r_1 = 11/3 toward 2+sqrt(3). Chain vertices with d <= H: O(log H). For j >= 2 (c_j >= 3), v_j has exactly 2 children: v_{j+1} and u_j; every a=b=1 vertex lies on this chain.

(ii) ab is nondecreasing along child edges. Mutating x in {a,b,c}: x' > d is the new max, so the child's two smallest entries are the two smallest of {a,b,c,d}\{x}: mutate a gives bc >= ab; mutate b gives ac >= ab; mutate c leaves ab.

(iii) The unique off-chain child of v_j (j >= 2) is u_j = (1,c_j,d_j,4c_jd_j - 1), max m_j = 4c_jd_j - 1 >= 12d_j - 1 >= 11d_j; its ab = c_j >= 3, so by (ii) every vertex of subtree(u_j) has ab >= 3 and every edge below multiplies the max by >= 4ab - 1 >= 11. The subtrees subtree(u_j), j >= 2, are pairwise disjoint (tree, distinct parents), disjoint from the chain (there b >= 3), and every vertex lies on the chain or in exactly one of them (descend to the root; the path leaves the chain at most once, since ab >= 3 is irreversible by (ii)).

(iv) Subtree count. Vertices of subtree(u_j) with max <= H sit at depth <= log_{11}(H/m_j) below u_j, <= 3 children each, so size <= sum_k 3^k <= (3/2)*3^{log_{11}(H/m_j)} = (3/2)(H/m_j)^rho with rho = ln3/ln11 = 0.4582 < 1/2.

(v) Summation. m_j >= 11 d_j and d_j >= 11*(11/3)^{j-2} (induction: d_{j-1} <= (3/11)d_j, so d_{j+1} = 4d_j - d_{j-1} >= (41/11)d_j >= (11/3)d_j). Hence sum_{j>=2} m_j^{-rho} <= 121^{-rho} / (1 - (11/3)^{-rho}) = 0.248, convergent since (11/3)^rho = 1.814 > 1. Therefore N(H) <= C*H^rho + O(log H), rho = ln3/ln11 = 0.4582, C = (3/2)*sum_{j>=2} m_j^{-rho} <= 0.372, an effective constant. N(H) = O(H^{0.4582}), sublinear; rq1 resolved by Outcome A.

CORRECTION to skeleton (v): d_j >= 11(2+sqrt3)^{j-2} is false (r_j increases to 2+sqrt3 from below); the explicit base 11/3 is used instead, with all conclusions unchanged.

Depth extremes: the chain is the unique slowest branch (asymptotic factor 2+sqrt3), so chain depth = log_{2+sqrt3}(d) + O(1); T1's log_3 is approached only through the root's small factors, and T3's lower bound is approached along branches maximizing each factor (child max ~ 4d^3 requires a,b,c comparable to d).

LABELED OBSERVATION (hand-checkable substitution, not an enumeration): struct-core-v2 O1-O3 realize v_1, v_2, and u_2 = (1,3,11,131) with m_2 = 4*3*11 - 1 = 131 >= 11*11 and 1+9+121+17161 = 17292 = 4*4323 confirms u_2 in S; it has ab = 3, so its descendants grow by factor >= 11 as claimed.

STATUS: T1, T2, T3, T4 PROVED; rq1 closed by Outcome A with explicit exponent rho = ln3/ln11 and effective constant C <= 0.372; no conjecture remains open in this thread.
assumptions: Tree structure, descent, and per-edge factor >= 3 are taken as proved from answer:work:003-struct-core-v2 (L1, L2, L3, D1-D3); the lemmas used are restated in one line each in the account.
Height means maximum coordinate d (C3); permutations are identified (C6).
No external corpus exists (SC6); all content is first-principles derivation, with board citations for the previously proved structural lemmas.

boundary_findings.consequence_if_absorbed: Quoting the skeleton's inequality verbatim would embed a false lemma in the memorandum; instead the valid explicit base 11/3 replaces it, preserving the convergence argument, the exponent rho = ln3/ln11, and the effective constant.
boundary_findings.narrative: The assigned packet skeleton contained one incorrect intermediate inequality (d_j >= 11(2+sqrt3)^{j-2}), incompatible with the chain recurrence whose ratios increase to 2+sqrt(3) from below.

claims.statement: T1: every child edge multiplies the maximum coordinate by >= 3, hence d >= 3^{depth(v)} and depth(v) <= log_3 d for every vertex v.
T2: N(H) <= (3^{floor(log_3 H)+1} - 1)/2 <= (3H-1)/2 = O(H) with explicit constant 3/2, using <= 3 children per vertex and exactly 1 child of the root.
T3: child max <= 4d^3, so L_k = max log_2 d at depth k satisfies L_k <= 3^k - 1, giving depth(v) >= log_3(log_2 d + 1); two-sided relation log_3(log_2 d + 1) <= depth(v) <= log_3 d.

T4 dichotomy proved: (i) the a=b=1 locus is exactly the chain v_{j+1} = (1,1,d_j,4d_j-c_j) with d_{j+1}=4d_j-d_{j-1}, ratio increasing from 11/3 to 2+sqrt(3), contributing O(log H) vertices with d <= H; (ii) the product ab of the two smallest coordinates is nondecreasing along every child edge (three one-line cases); (iii) the unique off-chain child of v_j (j>=2) is u_j = (1,c_j,d_j,4c_jd_j-1) with m_j >= 11 d_j and ab = c_j >= 3, so every edge in subtree(u_j) multiplies the max by >= 11; these subtrees are disjoint and together with the chain partition S.

counterevidence: Skeleton step (v) claimed d_j >= 11(2+sqrt3)^{j-2}, which is false because the ratios r_j = d_{j+1}/d_j increase toward 2+sqrt(3) from below (r_1 = 11/3 < 2+sqrt3); the proof here uses the explicit valid base 11/3, and the convergence and exponent are unaffected.
claims.statement: T4(iv)-(v): subtree(u_j) contributes <= (3/2)(H/m_j)^rho vertices with max <= H, rho = ln3/ln11 = 0.4582 < 1/2; since m_j >= 11 d_j >= 121*(11/3)^{j-2}, the sum over j >= 2 of m_j^{-rho} converges to <= 0.248, giving N(H) <= C*H^rho + O(log H) with effective constant C = (3/2)*sum_{j>=2} m_j^{-rho} <= 0.372. N(H) = O(H^{ln3/ln11}), sublinear; rq1 Outcome A.

Depth extremes: the chain is the unique slowest infinite branch, with asymptotic edge factor 2+sqrt(3) (so chain depth = log_{2+sqrt3}(d) + O(1)); T1's log_3 upper depth bound is approached only via the root's small factors; T3's lower bound is approached along branches maximizing each factor (child max comparable to 4d^3, requiring a,b,c comparable to d).

Labeled observation (hand-checkable substitution, not an enumeration): u_2 = (1,3,11,131) satisfies 1+9+121+17161 = 17292 = 4*1*3*11*131, has m_2 = 4*3*11 - 1 = 131 >= 11*11 and ab = 3, instantiating T4(iii); v_1 = (1,1,1,3), v_2 = (1,1,3,11) instantiate the chain recurrence.

counterevidence: Skeleton step (v) contained a false inequality (base 2+sqrt3 for d_j); corrected to base 11/3. Flagged so the flawed line is not propagated.

T1's factor 3 is never asymptotically attained on any branch (chain factor tends to 2+sqrt(3) > 3); the log_3 depth bound is therefore not sharp, but it is exactly what was requested and is superseded in sharpness by T4's dichotomy, not contradicted.

No counterexample found to the dichotomy: the only vertices with ab <= 2 are the chain vertices (ab=1); u_1 coincides with the chain child at j=1 since b=c=1 there. Verified structurally via the a=b=1 descent, not merely by spot checks.

knowledge_links.rationale: Proves T1-T3 with explicit constants, the full dichotomy (i)-(iii), and the sublinear bound N(H) = O(H^{ln3/ln11}) with effective constant, meeting the acceptance condition (Outcome A).
Strongest attained rigorous upper bound: N(H) <= C*H^rho + O(log H), rho = ln3/ln11 = 0.4582, C <= 0.372 effective, superseding the crude O(H).
Two-sided depth relation log_3(log_2 d + 1) <= depth(v) <= log_3 d proved, with the chain identified as the slowest branch (depth log_{2+sqrt3} d + O(1)).
Proves the slow/fast dichotomy: slow growth confined to the explicit chain (O(log H) vertices), all other branches grow by factor >= 11 per edge; concludes sublinear exponent, rq1 Outcome A.

objective: D4+D6+rq1: Prove the strongest rigorous upper bound for N(H) and the two-sided depth-vs-log-H relation for the rooted tree of sorted solutions of a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=4abcd. REQUIRED SKELETON (terse lemma-proof, HARD CAP 700 words, no tables, no digressions): Restate in one line each, citing as proved: mutation at max d strictly lowers d; mutations at a,b,c raise max to >= (4ab-1)d >= 3d; quotient graph is a tree rooted at (1,1,1,1); every vertex has <= 3 children, root has 1. (T1, depth upper) d >= 3^depth so depth <= log_3 d. (T2, crude upper) N(H) <= sum_{k<=log_3 H} 3^k <= (3H-1)/2 = O(H), explicit constant. (T3, depth lower) child max <= 4 d^3, so inductively log2(max at depth k) <= 3^k - 1, giving depth >= log_3(log2 d + 1); state the two-sided relation log_3(log_2 d+1) <= depth <= log_3 d. (T4, rq1 dichotomy — the main sharpening) Prove: (i) a=b=1 forces the vertex onto the chain: (1,1,c,d) satisfies c^2+d^2+2=4cd, and by the same descent argument all its solutions form the single chain v_0=(1,1,1,1), v_1=(1,1,1,3), v_{j+1}=(1,1,d_j,4d_j-c_j); chain ratio tends to 2+sqrt(3), so #chain vertices with d<=H is <= log_{2+sqrt3}(H)+O(1) = O(log H). (ii) Along any child-path (height-increasing), the product ab of the two smallest coordinates is nondecreasing (mutating a,b,or c replaces one of them by a larger value; check the three cases in one line each). (iii) The unique off-chain child of chain vertex v_j (j>=2, i.e. c_j>=3) is u_j=(1,c_j,d_j,4c_jd_j-1) with max m_j=4c_jd_j-1 >= 3 d_j; it has ab=c_j>=3, so by (ii) every descendant edge multiplies the max by >= 4*3-1=11. (iv) Subtree of u_j down to max<=H has depth <= log_{11}(H/m_j) and <= 3 children per vertex, hence size <= (3/2)*(H/m_j)^rho with rho=log 3/log 11 (=ln3/ln11, approx 0.458 < 1/2). (v) Sum over j>=2: since d_j >= 11(2+sqrt3)^{j-2}, sum_j m_j^{-rho} converges to an explicit constant; conclude N(H) <= C*H^rho + O(log H) with rho=log3/log11, i.e. N(H)=O(H^rho) sublinear — state C explicitly if cheap, else as an effective constant. If any step resists, prove what holds and label the rest CONJECTURE with the exact gap. STRICT BREVITY: symbol-dense lemma-proof style; omit prose motivation entirely.

raised_questions.acceptance_condition: Either a proved improvement N(H) = O(H^{rho'}) with rho' < ln3/ln11, or a proved lower bound N(H) >= c*H^beta for some beta > 0 that brackets the exponent, or a rigorous statement that branching-3 with factor exactly 11 occurs along a positive-density set of branches (making rho sharp for this method).
discriminating_outcomes: Improved exponent rho' < 0.4582 proved: the minimal-factor-11 assumption is shown to be density-zero, so the subtree sizes are o((H/m_j)^rho).
Positive lower bound beta > 0 proved: N(H) is genuinely polynomial, bracketing alpha in [beta, 0.4582].
A family of vertices with ab = 3 and factor exactly 11 at positive density: rho is sharp for this method and further progress needs a new invariant.
raised_questions.rationale: The upper bound treats each fast subtree as a worst-case 3-ary tree with minimal factor 11; both assumptions are generically far from tight, so the exponent 0.4582 is an artifact of the method. The most informative next mathematical step is quantifying typical branching and typical factor inside one fast subtree.
raised_questions.text: Is the exponent rho = ln3/ln11 = 0.4582 improvable toward the true growth rate of N(H)? Specifically: inside subtree(u_j), bound how often vertices have the full 3 distinct children versus equal-coordinate coincidences, and how the per-edge factor (>= 11, typically much larger) distributes; combine with the lower-bound thread to decide whether N(H) = Theta(H^alpha) for some alpha or whether the true growth is polylogarithmic-times-subpower.

unresolved: Sharpness of rho = ln3/ln11: the bound uses worst-case 3-ary branching and the minimal factor 11 inside fast subtrees; typical behavior is likely much sparser, so rho is an upper-bound artifact (see raised question rq-sharp).
The constant C <= 0.372 is effective but loose; tightening it requires exact values of m_j and exact subtree counts, neither of which affects the exponent.
The lower-bound side (D5) is a separate thread (work:004-lower-bound-v3); combining it with rho is needed before any Theta-conjecture can be framed under D8.
